item.title: Ichijodani Asakura Clan Ruins: A Reconstructed Sengoku-Era Castle Town — Guide
item.description: Ichijodani was the thriving castle town of the powerful Asakura clan during the Sengoku period, ruling much of the surrounding region for over a century before Oda Nobunaga’s forces destroyed the town in 1573, after which it was largely abandoned and buried, preserving the site remarkably intact beneath the soil for centuries. Extensive excavation since the 1960s has revealed samurai residences, gardens and merchant streets, and a partially reconstructed street of period buildings now lets visitors walk through a physical recreation of Sengoku-era daily life, one of the most complete such reconstructions in Japan.
